title: Entropy and the arrow of time
researchPrompt: The laws of physics are almost all time-symmetric, yet time clearly runs one way. Explain how entropy is used to account for that, and what the account still leaves unexplained.
suggestedAngles: Distinguish microstates from macrostates and let the counting argument do the work
Treat it as a statistics problem rather than a physics one
Confront the past hypothesis: why the low-entropy start is assumed, not derived

title: How CRISPR finds one sequence in a genome
researchPrompt: Explain how a CRISPR-Cas9 complex locates a specific 20-base sequence among billions, and why off-target edits happen at all.
suggestedAngles: Follow the guide RNA as the addressing mechanism and Cas9 as the tool
Explain the PAM requirement as a search filter that makes the problem tractable
Use the off-target failure mode to show the matching is tolerant, not exact

title: Why antibiotic resistance is an evolutionary certainty
researchPrompt: Explain why resistance emerges as a predictable consequence of using antibiotics at all, rather than as a failure of any particular drug.
suggestedAngles: Frame the antibiotic as a selection pressure rather than a weapon
Use generation time to explain why bacterial evolution is observable in a hospital ward
Separate the biology from the policy question of stewardship
